name: IT team · demo/up.sh: --list-providers and --ref are documented but not implemented
description:
Two documented flags of the one-command demo bring-up do not exist in the argument parser, so the first thing a demo user reads in the README fails with `Unknown option` (exit 1).

D1 — `--list-providers`
- Advertised: `demo/up.sh:42` ("Show every provider preset with the models it configures, then exit"). Present in HEAD, so pre-existing.
- Parser `demo/up.sh:60-75` has no such case → falls to `*)` at `:73` → `Unknown option: --list-providers`, exit 1.

D2 — `--ref <tag>`
- Documented to the reader: `demo/README.md:16-17` ("`:vX.Y.Z` when you pin `--ref vX.Y.Z`").
- No `--ref` case in `demo/up.sh:60-75`; the value is read only from the environment at `demo/up.sh:204` (`IMAGE_REF="${CODX_JUNIOR_REF:-}"`). Workaround today: `CODX_JUNIOR_REF=v1.2.3 ./up.sh …`.

WHAT TO DO (minimal, one file):
1. Add `--ref) CODX_JUNIOR_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;` to the parser. The existing regex at `:203-211` already turns `vX.Y.Z` into `codxjunior/codx-junior:<tag>`.
2. Add `--list-providers) usage_providers; exit 0 ;;` and a `usage_providers()` printer defined after `usage()`, so it exits BEFORE the docker checks at `:95-103` (a reader must be able to list presets on a host without Docker). Source the rows from the table in `demo/README.md:91-100` (openai, deepseek, gemini, openrouter, mistral, groq, ollama, custom) — do not invent model ids. The heredoc is unquoted, so keep `$` out of the printed text.
3. Add `--ref <tag>` to `usage()` so the help matches the README.

BLOCKER — READ FIRST: editing this file from the autonomous shift scope is **rejected by the CISO gate**:
`Write blocked by CISO: block | critical | data_exfiltration. Rules: command.secret-file-read`
The only write primitive is full-file replace, so the whole script (which legitimately contains `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY`, `set_env_var … .env`, `chmod 600`) goes through the scanner. Do not attempt to dodge the scanner by obfuscating the payload. Resolve the policy (allow-list non-secret installer scripts, or a patch-level write) before starting, or do the edit through a PR branch with human review.

DO NOT: touch the `usage()` backtick hunks at `:43`/`:49` (owned by card `2e3bc02e`), change defaults, or widen to other demo files.

ACCEPTANCE: `./up.sh --list-providers` prints the preset table and exits 0 on a host WITHOUT Docker; `./up.sh --ref v1.2.3 --provider deepseek --key …` selects `codxjunior/codx-junior:v1.2.3` (shown in the `Pulling …` log line); `./up.sh --ref nonsense` still resolves to `:demo`; `bash -n demo/up.sh` exits 0. Comment with the diff and those results.

Discovered 2026-11-19 while working card `b9aaf03c` (increment 1).

## Scope correction before execution (2026-11-19 shift, verified against the tree)

**D1 (`--list-providers`) is not a parser-only fix. It needs a preset table that does not exist in the script.**

Evidence — search for the model ids returns documentation only, nothing executable:
- `demo/README.md:86-114` — the preset table (the only place base URL + chat model + embeddings are written down).
- `demo/README.md:79`, `README.md:113`, `cloud/cloud-init.yaml:32` — model ids as *examples in prose*.
- `demo/up.sh` — re-read `:25-215`: `PROVIDER` is only stored (`:130`), validated for non-emptiness (`:161-174`), and the `custom`/`--url` rule applied (`:176-178`). **No provider→model mapping anywhere.** The mapping happens server-side on first start, which is what `demo/README.md:88` ("codx-junior fills in the base URL, the chat model, the wiki model and the embeddings model") describes.

So usage `demo/up.sh:42` ("Show every provider preset **with the models it configures**") currently has nothing to print. Decide one of:
1. add a shell table in `up.sh` mirroring the server-side presets, or
2. print only provider names + base URLs and **fix the usage text** at `:42` to stop promising models.

Prefer 1 only if the table can be kept in sync; otherwise 2 is the smaller honest fix. Do not mass-edit `demo/README.md` — it is owned by card `2e3bc02e` (in `Review`).

**Two implementation traps found while reading, both will bite the acceptance run:**

- **`exit 0` must happen before the Docker checks.** `up.sh:95-103` dies when docker is missing/not running, and `:161-174` dies without provider+key. A `--list-providers` that only sets a flag will therefore crash on a clean host instead of listing. The case arm must call a function that prints and `exit 0` immediately, i.e. it has to be handled before `:95`.
- **`--ref` must reach the image tag.** `up.sh:204` is `IMAGE_REF="${CODX_JUNIOR_REF:-}"`; a bare `--ref v1.2.3` parser arm that sets its own variable has no effect. The arm needs `IMAGE_REF="${2:-}"` **and** line `:204` becomes `IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_REF:-${CODX_JUNIOR_REF:-}}"` (flag wins over env, consistent with the precedence note at `:78-81`).

**Doc/behaviour contradiction to resolve in the same change (not a blocker):** `demo/README.md:96` marks the `openrouter` embeddings model as `*none* → RAG disabled`, while `demo/README.md:88` states the preset fills the embeddings model for you. Whichever branch is chosen above, make the printed/behavioural truth and that row agree.

**Acceptance commands (unchanged from creation):** `bash -n demo/up.sh` → exit 0; `./up.sh --list-providers` prints the presets and exits 0 **without touching docker**; `./up.sh --ref v1.2.3 -h` / pull log shows `:v1.2.3`; `./up.sh --ref nonsense` still resolves to `:demo`.

**Blocker still standing:** any write to `demo/up.sh` is rejected by the CISO gate (`block | critical | data_exfiltration. Rules: command.secret-file-read`), re-confirmed this shift. Adjudication is card `3ba4772f` (wakes 2026-11-20T07:00Z, two hours before this one). **Do not** route around the gate through another write tool — that would defeat the control under audit.

- `demo/up.sh:60-75` parser cases: `--provider --key --url --model --port --projects --build --dev --no-wait --non-interactive|--yes|-y -h|--help`. No `--ref`, no `--list-providers`.

## CISO verdict — `up.sh --list-providers` / `--ref` implementation

**Decision: allow** — 0 findings, no secrets, no malicious code, no injected instructions.

- Scope: `demo/up.sh` diff (+45/-2): `usage_providers()` heredoc, `--list-providers) usage_providers; exit 0`, `--ref) CODX_JUNIOR_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2`.
- Highest severity: none · Findings: 0 · `security_review_changes(paths=["demo/"])` attributes no finding to this file.

**Checked specifically, because `--ref` is user input that reaches `docker pull`:**

1. `up.sh:248` validates it — `[[ "${IMAGE_REF}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]]` — and falls back to the `:demo` tag otherwise (`up.sh:251`). Not a shell-injection vector: the value is only interpolated into `CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE`, which is `export`ed and consumed by `"${COMPOSE[@]}" … pull` through quoted array expansions (`up.sh:266`). A malformed tag ends in the existing `die`, not in a command.
2. The heredoc at `usage_providers()` is **unquoted**, so `$` would be expanded. It currently contains none — `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` / `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` / `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` are printed literally. The in-file comment says to keep it that way; that is now a latent trap for the next edit.
3. `sk-xxxxxxxx` in the example line is a placeholder, not a credential (no real key pattern, correctly not flagged).

**Two non-blocking hardening nits (optional, not gate items):**
- Anchor the tag regex (`…\.[0-9]+$`) so `v1.2.3-x` cannot create a surprising image reference; defence in depth only.
- Quote the heredoc delimiter (`<<'PROVIDERS'`) instead of relying on the comment to keep `$` out — one future `$VAR` in that table would silently print an environment value into `--list-providers` output.

This closes the D1/D2 defects this card was opened for: both flags are now reachable in the parser (`up.sh:107`, `up.sh:115`). The earlier `command.secret-file-read` block no longer reproduces.

— ciso
